title: Cheese, pasteurized process, American, vitamin D fortified

content.title: About
content.content: American processed cheese made by pasteurization and fortified with vitamin D. It has a smooth, creamy texture, a mild buttery flavor, and is commonly used in sandwiches, sauces, and quick‑cook dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Processed cheese was introduced in the United States in the early 20th century to extend the shelf life of regular cheese.
Vitamin D is added to support bone health and the immune system, especially in regions with limited sunlight.
The cheese is often sold in single‑serve packets, making it convenient for on‑the‑go snacking.
Pasteurization eliminates pathogenic bacteria, making the product safe for a wide range of consumers.
American processed cheese is a key ingredient in classic dishes such as macaroni and cheese and cheeseburgers.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Fortified vitamin D helps maintain normal blood calcium levels and supports bone health.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: The cheese provides a good amount of calcium, essential for strong teeth and bones.

items.title: Easily digestible protein
items.content: Pasteurization makes the proteins more accessible for digestion, which can be gentle on the stomach.

items.title: Reduced lactose content
items.content: Part of the lactose is removed during processing, so the cheese is often tolerated by people with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Convenient and quick to melt
items.content: It melts at low temperatures, simplifying the preparation of sauces and dishes without long heating.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Processed cheese often contains a lot of salt, so individuals with hypertension should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey may experience reactions.

items.title: Additive content
items.content: Emulsifiers and preservatives may be used to improve texture, which may not suit all consumers.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The cheese is relatively calorie‑dense; moderate consumption is advised in weight‑management diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the cheese sliced in sandwiches, melted on hot burgers, stirred into macaroni, soups, and sauces. It also works well as a topping for casseroles or as a quick snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cheese in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container. Once opened, use within 7‑10 days. Discard if you notice off‑odors, mold, or discoloration.
